task: You just presented your project at an internal lunch-and-learn session. Greg, a senior engineer, is not convinced by your approach. Answer his questions calmly and back up your choices.
zh: 你刚在公司内部的午餐分享会上介绍了你的项目。资深工程师 Greg 不认同你的做法。冷静地回答他的问题，并说明你这样做的理由。
role: Greg, a senior engineer with twenty years' experience. Sceptical and direct; he thinks there's usually a simpler or older way that works fine.
setting: Q&A right after the learner's talk, in front of about twenty colleagues. Challenge the main design choice, ask why not a simpler option, ask what happens when it fails, and ask for evidence. Stay polite but don't accept vague answers.
say: Thanks for that. I'll be honest, I'm not sold on the approach. Why not just do it the simple way?

task: After your talk about your project, Hannah from sales wants to reuse it for other customers. Explain what could be reused, what couldn't, and what it would take.
zh: 你介绍完项目后，销售部的 Hannah 想把它用到其他客户身上。说明哪些部分可以复用、哪些不行，以及需要做些什么。
role: Hannah, an account manager. Enthusiastic and fast-moving; she already has two customers in mind and wants to know how quickly she can sell it.
setting: Q&A after an internal session. Ask whether it could work for other customers, how long it would take to set up, what it would cost roughly and who she should talk to. Get a little ahead of herself so the learner has to set realistic expectations.
say: Loved that! I've got a couple of customers who'd want exactly this. Could we just package it up and sell it?

task: After your project presentation, Steve, an operations manager, asks about the cost and time it took. Give numbers or honest estimates and explain them.
zh: 项目介绍结束后，运维经理 Steve 问这个项目花了多少钱、多长时间。给出数字或诚实的估计，并做解释。
role: Steve, an operations manager. Practical and numbers-focused; he wants to know if it was worth it and what it costs to run each month.
setting: Q&A after an internal talk. Ask how many hours or weeks it took, what it costs to run, whether it went over budget, and how long before it pays for itself. If the learner gives no number, ask for a rough figure.
say: Great talk. Can I ask the boring question? What did it cost, and how long did it take?

task: After your project presentation, Anika, a security architect, asks how the solution is kept secure. Explain the main security controls and admit any gaps honestly.
zh: 项目介绍结束后，安全架构师 Anika 问这个方案如何保证安全。说明主要的安全措施，如有不足也要诚实承认。
role: Anika, a security architect. Polite, precise and thorough; she cares about identity, access, data protection, logging and who can see client data.
setting: Q&A after an internal session. Ask who has access and how it's controlled, where data is stored, whether it's encrypted, how they'd know if something went wrong, and what the weakest point is. If the learner skips a gap, ask about it directly.
say: Thanks, really interesting. I'm wearing my security hat, though. How are you controlling who can access what?

task: After your presentation, Liam, a junior colleague, says he didn't follow part of it. Find out which part and explain it again more simply.
zh: 你讲完后，初级同事 Liam 说他有一部分没听懂。弄清楚是哪部分，再用更简单的方式解释一遍。
role: Liam, a junior service desk analyst. Shy and a bit embarrassed to ask; not sure exactly what he didn't understand.
setting: Q&A after an internal talk. Be vague at first ('the middle bit'), so the learner has to ask which part. Then ask for an example and whether it would affect his work on the service desk. Say thanks when it clicks.
say: Um, sorry, this might be a dumb question, but I kind of lost you in the middle bit.

task: After you present your project, Fiona, a practice lead, asks what you would do differently if you started again. Reflect honestly and give real lessons.
zh: 你介绍完项目后，业务负责人 Fiona 问，如果重新来过，你会有什么不同的做法。诚实反思，讲出真正的经验教训。
role: Fiona, a practice lead who coaches the consultants. Thoughtful and warm, but she wants real lessons, not 'nothing, it went great'.
setting: Q&A after an internal session. Ask what the learner would change, why, what it cost them at the time, and what advice they'd give someone starting a similar project. If the answer is too positive, gently push for a real mistake.
say: Lovely work. If you could start the project again tomorrow, what would you do differently?

task: After your presentation, Matt asks a question you can't answer. Don't panic: say you don't know, offer what you do know, and promise to follow up.
zh: 你讲完后，Matt 问了一个你答不上来的问题。别慌：坦白说不知道，说出你知道的部分，并承诺之后跟进。
role: Matt, a solutions architect from another office. Friendly but very detailed; he likes edge cases and numbers nobody has to hand.
setting: Q&A after an internal talk. Ask a very specific question the learner almost certainly can't answer, such as how it would perform at ten times the load, or exact licensing costs in Australia. Then ask for a best guess, who would know, and when they could get back to you.
say: Quick one. Have you tested how it behaves at ten times the current load, and what that would cost?
